Marnus Labuschagne’s 48‑Inning Century Drought Sets Australian Record as South Africa Test Highlights Emerging Talent

28 Oct 2026, 11:22 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

4 min read

Record‑breaking drought for a former star

Marnus Labuschagne has now gone 48 consecutive Test innings without a century, the longest such run for any Australian top‑order batsman. The streak began after his last hundred at Old Trafford in the 2023 Ashes series. Since then his Test average has slipped to 24.77, a stark contrast to the 65.00 average he posted from his 2019 Ashes debut as a concussion substitute through to the end of England’s 2023 tour.

The Cape Town Test – a turning point?

In the second Test of the series against South Africa at Newlands, Cape Town, Australia were set a target of 330 runs to win. After a quick loss of Steve Smith to a neck injury, Labuschagne was promoted to the crucial number‑three slot. He survived five deliveries on day two before being dismissed without scoring – a duck that extended his century‑less run to a new Australian record.

South Africa posted 329/6 (Starc 6‑72) with Ackerman making 95. Australia, at 330‑4, held a one‑run lead when Labuschagne fell. The match later saw junior players Matt Renshaw (74), Cameron Green (65) and Josh Inglis (85*) forge a 145‑run partnership for the sixth wicket, steering Australia away from a potential collapse.

Former players weigh in

  • Jason Gillespie (former fast bowler) told ABC that the 48‑innings stretch “will never be broken” and suggested Australia may need to look beyond Labuschagne.
  • Ricky Ponting (former captain) earlier called for Labuschagne’s removal, remarking that “he can’t score off the back foot.”
  • Simon Katich (former batsman) on SEN Radio said the pressure on Labuschagne was “nerves and the pressure the selectors have put him under for an extended period of time.”

These comments reflect a growing consensus among ex‑players that Labuschagne’s prolonged slump is unusual for a player who once averaged near‑Bradman levels.

Emerging alternatives in the Australian line‑up

The Cape Town performance highlighted three younger batsmen who have begun to fill the void:

  • Matt Renshaw – previously on the fringes, his 74 in this Test follows a career‑best 190 in Durban and may cement his place for the winter.
  • Cameron Green – at 27, his 65 showed a composure that has often been questioned in his 39 previous Tests.
  • Josh Inglis – born in Yorkshire, he returned from a broken finger to score an unbeaten 85, demonstrating effective cutting and sweeping against South African spinners.

If Smith returns for the upcoming New Zealand series in December, Green and Inglis are likely to shift back to the middle order, leaving the number‑three slot open again.

What remains uncertain

  • Selection policy – Whether the Australian selectors will continue to give Labuschagne extended runs at number three or replace him with a younger option remains a decision for the coaching staff.
  • Long‑term form – Labuschagne’s technical issues, such as difficulty scoring off the back foot, have been highlighted, but no definitive analysis has been published by Cricket Australia.
  • Impact on the series – The outcome of the remaining Tests in South Africa will influence both the World Test Championship standings and the momentum of the emerging players.

Practical implications for fans and stakeholders

  • Team composition – A shift away from Labuschagne could see a more aggressive top order, potentially altering Australia’s approach against quality pace and spin attacks.
  • Player contracts – Continued poor form may affect Labuschagne’s central contract negotiations, while strong performances from Renshaw, Green and Inglis could enhance their bargaining position.
  • Future tours – The performances in South Africa will likely inform squad selections for the upcoming New Zealand series and the 2025 World Test Championship final.
